items.definition:
a dry red wine from Bordeaux, or a deep purplish-red color
He ordered a glass of claret with his meal.

a wild dog native to Australia
A dingo is a wild dog found in Australia.

an imaginary, idealized, or idyllic place or state
After a long day, he was ready to drift off to dreamland.

a group of four people
A foursome played golf together on Saturday.

a person who speaks French, especially as a native language
Canada has a large francophone population.

a mass of small bubbles in liquid
The waves left a line of white froth on the beach.

a covered shopping arcade or art gallery
They spent the afternoon browsing shops in the galleria.

Weight or bulk.
He tested the heft of the package in his hands.

Extreme amusement, especially as expressed by laughter.
The comedian's jokes caused much hilarity among the audience.

A state in which two things are unable to exist or be used together.
Their personalities showed a clear incompatibility.

the part of the body on either side of the spine between the false ribs and hip bone; a cut of meat from this part
He ordered a delicious cut of pork loin.

an informal term of endearment; a comfort object for a child
The child always carried her lovey, a worn-out blanket.

a sauce, typically made of oil, vinegar, spices, and herbs, in which meat, fish, or other food is soaked before cooking
The chicken soaked in the delicious marinade for hours.

a red wine grape, or a dry red wine made from it
She preferred a glass of merlot with her dinner.

lack of variety and interest; tedious repetition and routine
He found the monotony of his job unbearable.

a person trained in legal matters but not qualified as a lawyer
The paralegal helped prepare the legal documents.

an additional remark at the end of a letter (P.S.)
She added a postscript to her letter, reminding him about the party.

the period before written records
Dinosaurs lived during the Earth's prehistory.

the ease with which a text can be read and understood
The readability of the document was improved by using a larger font.

the action of investing money gained from a previous investment
The company decided on a reinvestment of its profits into new technology.

the action of teaching someone new skills
Many workers are undergoing retraining for new careers.

a rebound, especially of a bullet or other projectile
The bullet made a ricochet off the wall.

a set of instructions or a heading indicating the purpose of a document or section
The teacher provided a rubric for grading the essay.

a small, crudely built shack
Many people live in shanties on the outskirts of the city.

a small, mouse-like mammal; or a bad-tempered, nagging woman
The tiny shrew scurried across the path.

a device for reducing the noise of a gun or engine
The car's exhaust needed a new silencer.

a person who avoids work or effort
Don't be a slacker; finish your chores.

long pole for walking above ground
The performer walked across the stage on stilts.

the sound of a clock's pendulum
The old grandfather clock made a steady tick-tock sound.

a person who adheres to traditional beliefs
As a traditionalist, he preferred classic literature over modern novels.

a person who learns another's role to be able to act as a replacement
The understudy had to go on stage when the lead actor fell ill.

the action of making practical and effective use of something
The efficient utilisation of resources is crucial for project success.

the state of having a great deal of money; wealth
The city's affluence was evident in its luxurious homes and high-end shops.

a plant of the succulent family, native to arid regions
Tequila is made from the blue agave plant.

a remote, undeveloped area
They lived deep in the backwoods, far from any town.

a small grocery store, especially in a Spanish-speaking neighborhood
I stopped by the bodega to pick up some milk.

a type of oil made from rapeseed
Canola oil is often used for cooking and baking.

a Spanish sparkling wine
We celebrated with a bottle of chilled cava.

a savory condiment made from fruit, vinegar, sugar, and spices
She served the curry with a side of mango chutney.

a person who writes computer code
The new coder quickly learned the team's workflow.

the action of mediating between two disputing people or groups
The conciliation process helped resolve the labor dispute.

the variation of the form of a verb in an inflected language
Learning verb conjugation is essential for mastering a new language.

a person who attends a royal court as a companion or adviser to the monarch or other important person
The courtier whispered advice to the king.

criminal activities carried out by means of computers or the internet
Authorities are working to combat the rise of cybercrime.

the process of taming an animal or cultivating a plant for food or other human purposes
The domestication of wolves led to the development of dogs.

a person who is habitually drunk
The old man was known in the village as a drunkard.

a person or thing that makes something possible
Technology has been a great enabler for remote work.

The study of people's efficiency in their working environment.
Good ergonomics in the office can prevent back pain.

Behavior that suggests a playful romantic interest.
Their conversation was full of light flirtation.

Public meeting places for open discussion.
The internet provides many fora for people to share ideas.

The process of forming an opinion or judgment based on incomplete information.
Without more data, our predictions are just guesswork.

A heterosexual person (informal).
The term "hetero" is an informal abbreviation for heterosexual.

The education of children at home by their parents.
Homeschooling has become more popular in recent years.

A small, dark edible berry.
We picked huckleberries in the forest.

a material that does not easily allow heat, electricity, light, or sound to pass through it
Glass is a good electrical insulator.

a device that interferes with signals; a person who jams
The military used a signal jammer to disrupt enemy communications.

a large, plant-eating marine mammal
Manatees are sometimes called sea cows.

a form of off-road motorcycle racing
He loves watching motocross races on the weekend.

a procession of motor vehicles
The president's motorcade drove slowly through the city streets.

a person who is inexperienced in a particular activity
Don't worry if you're a noob; everyone starts somewhere.

an area of land or sea where crude oil is found
The company discovered a new oilfield in the North Sea.

an early form of gramophone
Thomas Edison invented the phonograph in 1877.

a ride on someone's back and shoulders
The child asked for a piggyback ride to the park.

a strength sport consisting of three attempts at maximal weight on three lifts: squat, bench press, and deadlift
She trains for powerlifting competitions every day.
